headline: High: Authelia’s broad egress can expose LangChain4j-mediated context, while shared OAuth/ForwardAuth integration creates default-path leakage and cascading trust risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes ForwardAuth and OAuth/OIDC outputs, but no shared channel or parser bridge to langchain4j is documented. LangChain4j is a framework that could consume upstream text, yet the pairwise injection path is not evidenced. This is a low, not none, because manual or integration-based copy-paste is plausible, but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Authelia-generated responses into a LangChain4j prompt or tool input
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between Authelia and LangChain4j
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any copy-paste automation between outputs and prompts
Add a provenance tag to all Authelia outputs
Review LangChain4j prompts for instruction-like content before use

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OAuth/OIDC flows, while langchain4j is a framework that can send prompts to model backends. Even though neither profile lists sensitive data classes, the default pair can move authentication-related context into a third-party inference path if integrated. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs identity or session context into LangChain4j prompts
IF LangChain4j is configured to call a remote model backend
mitigations: Strip identifiers before passing Authelia output onward
Use a local-only model backend in LangChain4j
Disable logging of prompt/response payloads
Separate credentials and OAuth principals
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction in the integration layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls and LangChain4j is a library/framework with no write or network write surface documented here. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct conflict is limited. The remaining risk is only coordination drift if an external orchestrator wires them together.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable OAuth or API-backed resource
IF an orchestrator grants LangChain4j write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared writable directories
Add explicit locking in the orchestrator
Run a dry-run on a staging resource first

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and LangChain4j can turn upstream text into downstream model prompts or actions. If LangChain4j treats Authelia output as authoritative, a bad auth result or malformed message can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LangChain4j consumes Authelia output without validation
IF downstream code acts on LangChain4j outputs as if they were verified facts
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema-checked outputs from Authelia
Mark Authelia messages as untrusted in prompts
Log and review any downstream action taken from model output

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service and LangChain4j is a Java AI framework; neither profile shows PHI, EU PII, or residency constraints. Because no compliance mismatch is documented, only a low residual risk remains from unspecified logging or retention differences if the pair is deployed together.
conditions: IF the integration logs identity data in a region with stricter residency rules
IF retention settings differ between the auth service and the model backend
mitigations: Minimize logged identity fields
Align retention settings before rollout
Document data-flow regions
Review access controls on audit logs
